用一束光，\n做一只钟。:
Make a clock
from a beam of light.
光波、光钟与光锥的连续场景。拖动画面可进入实验，改变相对速度。: A continuous scene of light waves, light clocks and light cones. Drag to enter the experiment and change relative speed.
画面未能绘制，请重新载入。: The scene could not be drawn. Please reload.
提高相对速度，运动钟的斜路变长、滴答变慢。换到另一艘船，每个人自己的钟都照常走。: Increase relative speed: the moving clock’s diagonal path lengthens and its ticks slow down. Change frames and each observer’s own clock still runs normally.
每个速度对应一个匀速实验: Each speed selects a constant-velocity experiment
提高速度，看光钟变慢: Increase speed and watch the light clock slow down
比较同一次发射与接收。换参考系，光走过的距离和用去的时间一起变，二者相除仍是 c: Compare the same emission and reception. Change frames and both the distance light travels and the time it takes change. Their ratio is still c.
距离 / 时间 = 1 光秒/秒 = c: Distance / Time = 1 light-second per second = c
光钟半程的勾股关系: Pythagorean relation for one leg of the light clock
两套坐标，距离除以时间相同: Different distances and times. The same ratio.
展开从下镜到上镜的半程。镜距、镜子位移与斜光路组成直角三角形；光走得越远，用时就: Unfold one leg from the lower mirror to the upper one. Mirror spacing, sideways motion and the diagonal light path form a right triangle. More distance takes more time.
你坐上飞船，追赶一束光。飞船越开越快，光在你那里会不会慢下来？我们从一把尺、一只: You board a ship and chase a beam of light. As your ship gets faster, will the light slow down in your measurements? Let’s start with a ruler and a clock.
跟着画面看，也可以暂停慢慢读: Follow the scene, or pause to read at your own pace
多快，\n要用尺和钟量。:
How fast?
Use a ruler and a clock.
看这个小球：走过 6 米，用了 3 秒。每秒走 2 米，这就是它的速度。测光速，: Watch the ball: it travels 6 meters in 3 seconds. That is 2 meters per second. To measure light’s speed, we also need a distance and a time.
看刻度上的小球，与旁边经过的秒数: Watch the ball on the ruler and the seconds beside it
追一只球，\n它会显得慢些。:
Chase a ball.
It moves away more slowly.
地面上，球每秒走 10 米，你每秒追上 6 米。球每秒只离你远 4 米。日常生活: On the ground, the ball travels 10 meters each second while you chase at 6. It moves away from you by just 4 meters each second. At everyday speeds, we subtract like this.
上下两条轨道，使用同一套地面的尺和钟: Both tracks use the same ground-based rulers and clocks
换成光，\n答案变了。:
Try it with light.
The answer changes.
你以光速的八成追光。用飞船自己的尺和钟测量，光仍每秒走约三十万公里。实验支持这个: You chase light at 80% of its speed. Using your ship’s own rulers and clocks, you still measure about 300,000 kilometers per second. Experiments support this surprising result.
地面测得 c · 飞船也测得 c: Ground measures c · Ship measures c
光在真空中一秒走过的距离，叫“一光秒”，约三十万公里。它是距离单位。接下来，用它: The distance light travels in one second in vacuum is one light-second: about 300,000 kilometers. It is a unit of distance. We will mark our rulers with it.
光秒是距离，就像公里；不是一种时间: A light-second measures distance, like a kilometer—not time
测速度，不能只盯着两个东西的间距。飞船用自己的尺和钟，地面用地面的。它们对距离和: Measuring speed takes more than watching the gap between two objects. The ship uses its own rulers and clocks; the ground uses its own. Their measurements of distance and time can differ.
下面先看看，为什么两只钟会不同步地滴答: First, let’s see why two clocks can tick at different rates
速度 = 这个观察者量出的距离 ÷ 时间: Speed = distance ÷ time, measured in the same frame
光在两面镜子之间来回。每次回到底部，就算一次“滴答”。先看两只一样的钟：镜距一样: Light bounces between two mirrors. Every return to the bottom counts as one tick. First, compare two identical clocks: the same mirror spacing, the same ticking.
蓝色留在实验室，金色跟着飞船: Blue stays in the laboratory; gold travels with the ship
镜子走了，\n光得斜着追。:
The mirror moves.
Light takes a diagonal.
现在让飞船匀速前进。从地面看，光往上走时，上面的镜子也在向前走。光要碰到它，就得: Now the ship moves at a steady speed. From the ground, the upper mirror moves forward while the light travels upward. To meet it, light must take a longer, diagonal path.
盯住金色光点：它必须和上镜在同一处相遇: Watch the gold pulse: it must meet the upper mirror
同样的镜距 · 更长的光路: Same mirror spacing · Longer light path
把半程拆开看：镜距 3 光秒，侧移 4 光秒，斜路长 5 光秒。船上量到 3 秒: Unfold half a tick: 3 light-seconds between mirrors, 4 sideways, and 5 along the diagonal. The ship measures 3 seconds; the ground measures 5. Same light speed, different elapsed times.
飞船速度 0.8c · 半程到上镜，来回才是一拍: Ship speed: 0.8c · This is one leg; a round trip makes one tick
船上的一秒，\n没有变难熬。:
A second aboard
still feels normal.
船上的人看自己的钟，一切正常。地面拿自己的钟去比较，才发现运动钟滴答更慢。这叫“: Aboard the ship, your own clock runs normally. Comparing with a ground clock reveals that the moving clock ticks more slowly. This is called time dilation.
地面经过 5 秒 · 船上经过 3 秒: 5 seconds on the ground · 3 seconds aboard
不只是\n镜子里的把戏。:
More than
a trick with mirrors.
换成原子钟，也能测到时间差。匀速飞行时，船上的人也会判断地面的钟慢：双方使用的“: Atomic clocks also show time differences. In steady motion, the ship can judge the ground clock to be slower too: each frame uses a different meaning of “simultaneous” for its comparison.
先记住：每个人自己的钟都正常；接着解释“同时”: Everyone’s own clock runs normally. Next: what does “simultaneous” mean?
运动没有一个公认的绝对静止背景: There is no agreed absolute background of rest
记录一件事，\n要写“哪里、几点”。:
Record an event:
where, and when?
一盏灯闪了一下。给这件事记下位置和时刻，就得到一个“事件”。图上的点，是一件事的: A lamp flashes. Record its position and time: you have an event. Each dot in the diagram is the address of something that happened, with both a place and a time.
下面比较闪光发生的时刻，不是眼睛看见它的时刻: We compare when flashes happen, not when someone sees them
事件 = 某处，某时，发生了一件事: An event = something happening at a place and time
两盏灯同闪，\n谁说了算？:
Two lamps flash.
Simultaneous for whom?
实验室两端的钟已经对好时，两盏灯同时闪光。飞船也用自己对好时的钟记录，却认为两次: Clocks at both ends of the laboratory are synchronized, and the lamps flash together. The ship records them with its own synchronized clocks—and assigns them different times.
已扣除光传到眼睛的延迟；这是记录时刻的差异: Light-travel delay to the eye is accounted for; the recorded times differ
同一对闪光 · 对“同时”有不同判断: Same two flashes · Different judgments of “simultaneous”
这张薄面，\n就是一份“现在”。:
This thin sheet
is one version of “now.”
薄面上的点，是一个观察者认为同时发生的事。换到运动的飞船，这份“现在”就斜过去了: Points on the sheet are events one observer calls simultaneous. Switch to the moving ship and its “now” tilts. This links measurements of time and position.
格线是我们画的坐标，不是宇宙里真实的网: The grid is our coordinate system, not a physical net in space
距离变了，\n时间也一起变。:
Distance changes.
Time changes with it.
只看同一次发射和接收。地面量出 1 光秒、1 秒；飞船量出 0.5 光秒、0.5: Compare the very same emission and reception. The ground measures 1 light-second in 1 second; the ship measures 0.5 in 0.5. Dividing each distance by its time gives the same light speed.
飞船速度 0.6c · 两地时刻由各自参考系中对好时的钟记录: Ship speed: 0.6c · Each frame uses its own synchronized clocks at both places
把一圈圈光，\n叠成一段历史。:
Stack the circles.
See light’s history.
向上是更晚的时间；向旁边是更远的地点: Up means later; sideways means farther away
光锥 = 一次闪光的传播历史: A light cone = the history of a spreading flash
有些事，\n现在还来不及影响。:
Some events
are too soon to reach.
限制的是“某地、某时”这一件事，不是某地点永远去不了: The limit concerns a particular place and time, not a place forever out of reach
最早能到的时刻，由 c 决定: c sets the earliest possible arrival
光没有\n自己的静止座位。:
Light has
no seat at rest.
你不能坐进一个与光并排静止的参考系。所以不能说“光自己觉得一瞬间就到了”。图上的: You cannot occupy a reference frame that stands still alongside light. So we cannot say light “experiences an instant journey.” Emission and reception remain two different events.
数学上的零时空间隔，不等于零距离、同一事件: A zero spacetime interval does not mean zero distance or the same event
越接近，\n越难再快一点。:
Closer to c.
Harder to speed up.
给有质量的飞船增加能量，它会变快。但越接近 c，同样的提速需要越多能量。要真正达: Give a massive ship more energy and it speeds up. Near c, the same increase in speed takes ever more energy. Reaching c would require infinite energy.
看金色轨迹逼近光锥边缘，却始终留在里面: Watch the gold path approach the cone’s edge while remaining inside
可以越来越接近，无法加速到 c: Ever closer is possible; accelerating to c is not
一直飞，\n为什么不用一直推？:
Why keep moving
without a push?
汽车要烧油，是在克服阻力。没有外力时，普通物体也会一直匀速运动。光同样不需要持续: A car burns fuel to overcome resistance. Without external forces, ordinary objects keep moving at constant velocity too. Light needs no continuing push, and a photon in vacuum never accelerates from rest.
动力改变运动；保持匀速不需要持续推力: A force changes motion; constant velocity needs no continuing push
没有静止质量 ≠ 没有能量或动量: Zero rest mass does not mean zero energy or momentum
光到底\n是什么在动？:
What is moving
when light travels?
画面中的起伏代表电场、磁场的变化。这种变化会传播、传递能量。量子理论把光的能量交: These oscillations represent changes in electric and magnetic fields. The changes propagate and transfer energy. Quantum theory describes light exchanging energy in individual quanta: photons.
波形画的是场的数值，不是光子的外形: The wave shows field values, not the shape of a photon
光是电磁波 · 光子是电磁场的量子: Light is an electromagnetic wave · A photon is a quantum of the field
遇到玻璃，\n材料也加入了。:
In glass,
the material joins in.
光的电场推动材料里的电荷振动。电荷产生的场再和光叠加，整体波形便走得慢一些。看玻: Light’s electric field drives charges in the material to oscillate. Their fields combine with the light, slowing the overall wave. Watch its crests crowd together inside the glass.
连续的集体响应，不是光子一站站停车再出发: A collective response, not photons stopping and restarting at each atom
这里玻璃内的相速度 = c ÷ 1.5: Here, the phase speed inside glass is c ÷ 1.5
变慢的是\n介质中的传播。:
What slows down
is propagation in matter.
光进入这块静止的透明玻璃，频率不变，波长缩短。离开玻璃又恢复。相对论中那个共同的: Entering this stationary, transparent glass, the light keeps its frequency but its wavelength shortens. On leaving, it recovers. The shared c in relativity is the speed in vacuum.
画面采用理想透明、无色散介质: The scene uses an ideal transparent, nondispersive material
真空中 c · 玻璃中约 ⅔c: Vacuum: c · Glass here: about ⅔c
这个数字取决于单位。用光秒量距离，光速就写成 1。现行“米”用光速来定义；这并没: That number depends on our units. Measure distance in light-seconds and light’s speed becomes 1. Today the meter is defined using c; that does not explain why different observers measure the same light speed.
数值怎样写，与自然界遵守什么规律，是两个问题: How we write the number and the physical law are separate questions
放到最小，\n时空会有像素吗？:
Zoom all the way in.
Does spacetime have pixels?
一些量子引力理论提出离散结构，但还没有实验定论。普朗克长度也不是已经发现的像素大: Some quantum-gravity theories propose discrete structures, but experiments have not settled this. The Planck length is not a discovered pixel size. Our grid only helps us draw coordinates.
时空是否连续，仍是开放问题: Whether spacetime is continuous remains an open question
理论提出了可能 · 实验尚未确认: A theoretical possibility · Not experimentally confirmed
光速，连着\n我们的钟和尺。:
Light speed links
our clocks and rulers.
你现在已经看到：速度来自钟和尺；换一个观察者，时间、距离和“同时”一起改变，光速: Speed comes from clocks and rulers. Change observer, and time, distance, and “now” change together while light speed stays the same. Relativity explains how they fit; why nature follows these laws has no final answer.
点“亲手试试”，改变速度，再换到飞船看一遍: Choose “Try it yourself,” change the speed, then switch to the ship
不同的钟与尺 · 同一个 c: Different clocks and rulers · The same c
同一束光，各用自己的尺和钟；c 指局部真空光速: The same light, measured with each frame’s own rulers and clocks; c refers to local vacuum light speed
画面放慢播放，让一次滴答看得见: The scene is slowed down so you can watch a tick unfold
一闪之后，光向外扩散。每个圆圈记录一个时刻。把晚一些的圆圈放高一些，就得到上半部: After a flash, light spreads outward. Each circle records one moment. Place the later circles higher, and the upper funnel appears: the future light cone.
从中间的发光点发信号，光沿上半部锥面前进，慢一些的物体走在里面。锥外的那个事件发: Send a signal from the bright center. Light travels up the upper cone; slower objects stay inside. That event outside happens too early for the signal to arrive. The same place might receive it later.
